- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 18-day history shows volatility, adjust forecast toward 20-day SMA or 30-day moving average.
- When sentiment is high and price is near 30-day high, model often overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–2% for next 5–7 days unless sentiment remains strong.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.2–0.6) and price is volatile, model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true trend, especially if sentiment is rising.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture it; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment >0.6 and price >30-day high.
- If sentiment is low and price is near 30-day low, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
